draft.title: Distribution channels
card: A distribution channel is the path a product takes from the business that makes it to the customer. It can be direct, or it can pass through middlemen.

A direct channel sells straight to the customer, such as through the business's own website or shop. An indirect channel uses wholesalers, who buy in bulk and sell to retailers, and retailers, who sell to customers.

Intensive distribution stocks a product in as many outlets as possible, which suits everyday items such as snacks and drinks. Selective distribution uses a limited number of chosen outlets in an area.
Exclusive distribution lets only one outlet in an area sell the product. It suits luxury or specialised goods.
draft.remember: Choose the path to the customer, then choose how many outlets will stock the product.

a.q: A drink company wants its bottled water in every supermarket, servo and kiosk. Which distribution method is it using?
a.why: Stocking the product in as many outlets as possible is intensive distribution. Selective distribution is tempting, but it limits the product to a few chosen outlets, which is not what the company wants.
a.clue: Count how many outlets the company wants.

b.q: Priya makes handmade leather watches in Hobart. She lets only one jeweller in each capital city sell them, to protect the brand's image. Which approach is she using?
opts: Direct distribution through her own website
b.why: Only one outlet in each area sells the watches, so this is exclusive distribution. It uses retailers, so it is not direct. It is not selective, because selective distribution allows a limited number of outlets in an area rather than just one.
b.clue: How many outlets sell the watches in each city?
